We study this dependence in periodically driven Rydberg atom chains under single- and bi-frequency driving. Using Floquet perturbation theory, we show that each spin flip is characterised by a single interference amplitude set by its local interaction shift, and that a state freezes only where the amplitudes of all its available flips vanish simultaneously. This picture accounts quantitatively for the shift and proliferation of freezing frequencies with interatomic spacing and for the response of entire families of initial states, which are sorted by a single local motif. Freezing is strong only within a window of spacings bounded by interaction tails on one side and nearest-neighbour excitation facilitation on the other, outside of which the advantage of bi-frequency driving is lost. In the regime of large detuning amplitude, where freezing points are numerous and the perturbative description is controlled, this window leaves almost no room for the PXP limit.

items.title: Observation of collective flatbands in hybrid Mie-grating THz metasurfaces
authors: Jie Ji, Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Siyan Zhou, Kehan Wang, Yuri Kivshar, Jaime G\'omez Rivas
items.summary: We propose a novel type of functional metasurfaces created by a hybridization of Mie resonators with high-index optical gratings. We demonstrate that such hybrid metasurfaces possess flatbands characterized by zero group velocity and strong energy localization. We experimentally observe the flatbands in free-standing terahertz (THz) metasurfaces, where dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators, forming the grating, mediate multipolar hybridization and provide a geometric control over collective resonances. Our THz near-field measurements with a dipole excitation uncover long-lived coherent oscillations associated with the quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonant modes, while a spatial mapping resolves the resonant electromagnetic response across the dielectric interconnections. We vary the grating width continuously to tune the hybrid magnetic-dipolar resonances and substantially enhance the quality factor (Q factor), while preserving the quasi-!atband dispersion. Complementary Bloch-resolved Purcell calculations reveal the substantial Purcell enhancement with increasing Q factor, followed by a trend towards saturation and highlighting the interplay between radiative confinement and local emitter-mode coupling. We believe our findings establish the engineering of dielectric interconnections in periodic lattices as a novel strategy for spectrally tuning high-Q flatbands in these metastructures, tailoring localized electromagnetic interactions in functional optical metasurfaces.

items.title: Dynamics of the Nuclear Envelope and Mitotic Spindle in Closed Mitosis
authors: Wilson Lough, Zachary R. Gergely, Eduardo Corona, Meredith D. Betterton
items.summary: During closed mitosis, large-scale deformation of the nuclear envelope is driven by the mitotic spindle and chromosomes contained within it. Previous models of closed mitosis have established that the spatial distribution of spindle-generated forces influences nuclear morphology, but have imposed axisymmetry and focused on equilibrium shapes. We introduce a three-dimensional biophysical model of nuclear envelope remodeling and spindle elongation that incorporates thermal fluctuations to examine how spindle-generated forces, chromatin distribution, and nuclear envelope elasticity control nuclear shape in fission yeast. The model reproduces features of both successful and aberrant nuclear shape change, including centering of mispositioned spindles, the dumbbell nuclear shape transition, and the formation of nuclear protrusions. A phase diagram of nuclear shape shows that insufficient spindle force produces elongated but undivided nuclei, while sufficiently large spindle forces produce either symmetric division or envelope tethers, depending on the size of the chromatin-envelope contact region. Near the boundary between symmetric division and tethering, nuclei develop asymmetric single-tether configurations. A reduced-order representation of the coupled envelope-spindle system shows a symmetry-breaking transition between symmetric and asymmetric nuclear shapes. Below a critical chromatin-envelope contact size, symmetric configurations lose stability during spindle elongation and thermal fluctuations drive nuclear shape trajectories toward one of two stable asymmetric configurations. These findings identify a growth-driven mechanical mechanism for spindle centering and alignment during early mitosis and reveal how asymmetric nuclear morphologies can arise during anaphase even in the absence of structural differences between the two spindle poles.

items.title: Cryogenic Luminescence Thermometry of Upconversion Micro- and Nanoparticles via Deep Learning
authors: Pablo Jos\'e Coria Ledo, Lina W\"olcken, Lucas R. Mendicino, Santiago Gliosca, M. Claudia Marchi, Marcos Illescas, Beatriz Barja, Christian Tom\'as Schmiegelow
items.summary: Luminescence thermometry with single or optically trapped particles is hampered by weak signals that fluctuate with alignment, collection efficiency, and excitation conditions and, for $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$-based probes, by the loss of sensitivity of the luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) at cryogenic temperatures. Here we use a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to predict the temperature directly from single emission spectra of $\mathrm{NaYF}_4{:}\mathrm{Yb}^{3+},\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ micro- and nanoparticles between $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $105\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and compare it with the standard LIR under adverse conditions deliberately reproduced with particle ensembles. From $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $30\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the 1D-CNN reduces the single-spectrum mean absolute error from $5.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $1.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and keeps its temperature uncertainty nearly constant down to the lowest temperatures, where Stark-component features remain temperature dependent while the LIR loses its sensitivity. Under deliberate optical misalignment, its error increases only from $0.58\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $0.88\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, whereas that of the LIR rises from $1.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $3.5\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The same approach reaches sub-degree accuracy ($0.21\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) over a narrow temperature window and a single calibration valid across different pump powers and wavelengths. These results establish 1D-CNNs as robust single-shot thermometers and a step toward fast thermometry of single and trapped particles.

items.title: MatHarness: Towards Long-Horizon Open-ended AutoResearch for Computational Materials Science
authors: Yanlin Fei, Lei Li, Shaolong Chen, Nazhou Liu, Xinmiao Yu, Madalina Ciobanu, Navan Preet Singh, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das
items.summary: Materials science research is a non-linear, long-horizon process. Existing scientific agents, however, largely rely on specific task execution or predefined workflows, rendering them brittle in open-ended settings. To bridge this gap, we present MatHarness, an agent harness designed for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research spanning the complete lifecycle from initial ideation to manuscript writing. MatHarness couples three mechanisms: execution robustness through pre-flight verification, expert-distilled skills, and just-in-time auditing; epistemic adaptability through persistent research artifacts and an evolving scientific mental model; and collective intelligence through a heterogeneous multi-agent round table under targeted human oversight. We evaluate MatHarness on adsorbate-induced surface segregation in Cu-Zn alloys, an open question in methanol-synthesis catalysis. Over a multi-week trajectory consuming roughly 10^3 GPU-hours (50 production DFT relaxations prescreened by 171 machine-learning-potential evaluations) the system revised its plan six times, recovered autonomously from failed calculations, and had an independent auditor overturn one of its own over-attributed claims before publication. Within the sampled metallic dilute-limit models, the validated DFT analysis supports an adsorbate-induced tendency toward greater surface Cu exposure at both composition endpoints, with facet- and coverage-dependent exceptions. These results were compiled into a complete manuscript with human involvement concentrated in specification, approval, and strategic steering gates. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/PrentisAI/pippin.

items.title: MagTrace: Tracing magnetic order through the evolving scientific literature
items.summary: Much of the research on magnetic materials starts from their magnetic order, but confirming it from the papers by hand can take hours, and curated databases can be incomplete and outdated. In this work, we build MagTrace, a language model agent that, given only a material's name, searches four literature databases, reads open access full text and reports the magnetic orders the current literature supports, each with a confidence score and citations a reader can check. We evaluate its performance on 18 materials against an answer key complied from published papers, compared with two other conditions that vary in level of retrieval. On a score from 0 to 1 that combines correctness, detail, whether the most confident order is current, and citation integrity, MagTrace scores 0.839; the same underlying language model scores 0.676 given the abstracts from one literature search and 0.548 answering from memory. With a single search, the model finds the right kind of order but omits the propagation vector, which describes how the pattern repeats through the material's crystal structure, in 85% of its orders. From memory, the model often cites titles that lead to no indexed paper (for 25% of the orders we could check), and when a cited paper exists and has an abstract, the abstract contradicts the claim for 17% of those citations, against 7% for MagTrace.

items.title: Integrable Orbital Exchange between Ellipsoidally Deformed $p$, $d$, and $f$ Electron States: Two-Angle Sklyanin Representations and Fused Elliptic $R$-Matrices
items.summary: We construct integrable orbital exchange models from ellipsoidally deformed $p$, $d$, and $f$ multiplets. A two-angle realization of the Sklyanin algebra gives explicit Jacobi difference operators $D,L_i$, complete distortion spectra and eigenfunctions, and a positive inner product transported from Sklyanin's integral. In the $p$ sector the coordinate functions carry an exact spin-one action, and applying $D$ componentwise maps the confocal ellipsoid to a sphere. Elliptic fusion gives explicit $R$-matrices in the angular generators on both factors. Their Yang--Baxter relations yield commuting charges and exchange Hamiltonians for homogeneous and alternating chains, as well as mixed-pair interactions that can act between angular degrees of freedom on the same center. Exchange changes angular projections and correlations while preserving the two local Casimirs of each constituent, which fix its angular-momentum-squared and distortion-plus-rotation kinetic-energy invariants. The $p$--$p$ model recovers Fateev's elliptic spin-one interaction and reduces to the Takhtajan--Babujian Hamiltonian in the rational isotropic limit.

items.title: Distinguishing photothermal and photoelectrokinetic contributions to flow in light-activated microchannel architectures
authors: Sudharshan Anandan, Yuhang Fang, Lily Farmer, Maria Irineu, Shanmukhi Sripada, Tyler Hughes, Jared Nathan, Sathish Rajendran, Steven Wereley, Amy Marconnet, Thomas Beechem, Jeffrey L. Moran, David M. Warsinger
items.summary: Light-driven flows near Janus surfaces could power microfluidic devices without external hardware. These flows are often attributed to photoinduced electro- or diffusio-osmosis, but illumination also heats the surface, potentially driving natural convection. Here, we map flow and temperature around a UVA-illuminated TiO$_2$-Au Janus membrane using depth-resolved particle tracking and infrared thermometry. Recirculating rolls form on both sides, with no measurable net flow across the membrane. Their cubic, reversing velocity profile identifies horizontal (Hadley) convection, driven by a lateral temperature gradient as the gold film absorbs light. The measured profile agrees with wall-corrected Hadley theory using one fitted parameter. Adding 100 mM NaCl to suppress electrokinetic flows leaves the profile unchanged, indicating that convection dominates. Simulations show that convection falls below 1 $\mu$m/s in thin channels, where surface-driven osmotic flows could dominate. Thus, device geometry and surface chemistry determine which mechanism governs light-driven microfluidic flows.

items.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
authors: Athul S. Rema, Adri\'an E. Rubio L\'opez, Felipe Herrera
items.summary: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

items.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
authors: Kun Li, Tian Luo, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Yifeng Chen, Xinfu He, Yunquan Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu
items.summary: Material degradation emerges from microscopic events whose consequences accumulate over years, yet mechanism-resolved simulations remain confined below engineering timescales. The challenge is not just the sheer number of events: atomistic evolution is dominated by recurrent local motion, with only a tiny fraction driving lasting structural change. This distinction is not encoded in an instantaneous atomic configuration. Locally indistinguishable states can exhibit different event competition, escape times, and long-horizon outcomes, revealing missing kinetic context as a critical information bottleneck. This context spans space and time: the future consequence of a local transition depends on its surrounding defect environment and the kinetic history leading to its current state. To solve this, AtomWorld reconstructs a predictive kinetic state from multiscale structural observations and trajectory history, distinguishing transient fluctuations from microscopic pathways that drive persistent structural evolution. Learning operates only over transitions admitted by the underlying kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) process, preserving event legality, state evolution, and physical time. Across BCC Fe-Cu precipitation, FCC Ni-Cr-Al ordering, and HCP Zr-H interstitial transport, restoring kinetic context consistently advances persistent evolution while maintaining physical fidelity and transferring to unseen conditions. In irradiated reactor-pressure-vessel steel, this approach achieves up to 420-fold greater persistent evolution under matched event budgets. Combined with scalable execution, it successfully extends mechanism-resolved trajectories to service-year timescales across metre-scale heterogeneous domains.

items.title: Metastable states are precursors of Turing patterns in Adaptive Networks
items.summary: In networked reaction-diffusion systems, emergence of patterns from a homogeneous equilibrium can be described by Turing instability. Recently, Turing theory has been developed to include adaptive networks where, i.e., link weights change as a function of the states of the nodes. In this work we show that metastable states, defined as long living transient epochs with unique dynamical properties, could be observed in a range of parameters between Turing patterns and absence of any spatial pattern. Stated differently in the metastable regime the system ''switches'' between the homogeneous solution and the Turing pattern, never settling in any of those states, i.e., alternating silent and spiking regimes. By using phase diagrams and recurrence plots, we have numerically shown the existence of metastable states for the Brusselator model. Moreover, the dependence of the emergence of the metastable states on the adaptive control parameter has been characterized. The applicability of methods and ideas proposed in this work go beyond the considered case, they can help us in understanding conditions under which metastable states arise and could thus be informative to predict and control the latter.

items.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
items.summary: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU. We further extend our method to systems with large spin baths that lie beyond the reach of exact methods. Our approach thus offers a scalable and systematically improvable route to accurately simulate the decoherence dynamics of sensors in realistic spin environments.

items.title: Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise
authors: Zhuohang He, Qun Chen, Junjie Ma, Haochuan Zhang, Xiaojun Yuan
items.summary: We study extensive-rank matrix denoising for rotationally invariant signals corrupted by i.i.d. non-Gaussian noise. To exploit both the signal spectrum and the entrywise noise prior, we consider an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that alternates between a rotationally invariant spectral estimator and an entrywise denoiser. At each OAMP iteration, we conjecture a high-dimensional Gaussian equivalence property: the entrywise module admits an effective additive scalar Gaussian channel, whereas the spectral module behaves as if corrupted by i.i.d. Gaussian noise of matching variance. Under this conjecture, we formulate a state evolution (SE) recursion for the effective noise variances of both modules. Numerical simulations confirm that the SE predictions closely track the empirical mean-square errors. For robust principal component analysis (PCA), we apply this OAMP algorithm and characterize its recovery phase diagram via SE. Numerical results show that OAMP achieves a larger recovery region than several existing methods.

items.title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
authors: Xiongwei Guo, Fu Liu, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, Kuidong Wang
items.summary: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling. This work provides a novel method for realizing robust polarization-independent polaritons in bulk TMDCs metasurface and offers new insights for expanding the applications of polaritonic devices with arbitrary polarizations.

items.title: A Novel Algebraic Approach to Medium-Range Solvable Models
items.summary: We extend Jones' Baxterisation, which produces solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation directly from the generators of an algebra, to quantum spin chains with medium-range interactions. The key ingredient is an extended Yang-Baxter equation for R matrices that are built from the generators attached to two neighbouring sites. Together with the accompanying Lax operator, it gives rise to transfer matrices that are in involution up to boundary terms, exactly as in Jones' construction. We find a solution to the extended Yang-Baxter equation, of non-difference form, in terms of the generators of the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring, and obtain from it two families of medium-range lattice Hamiltonians. Thus, each representation of the algebra provides a medium-range solvable model. Using the relation between the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring and the fusion category $\mathrm{Rep}(S_3)$, we construct four such representations. They reproduce the folded XXZ model and the hard-rod deformed XXZ model, and give new medium-range models of a three-state antiferromagnet and of a Rydberg-blockade ladder. Two of the four models possess non-invertible symmetries.

items.title: High-temperature superconductivity from kinetic energy
authors: Hanbit Oh, Hui Yang, Ya-Hui Zhang
items.summary: Superconductivity is usually assumed to arise from attractive interaction. In this work we show that strong pairing is possible soley from kinetic energy even without a net attraction. We demonstrate a high-temperature kinetic superconductor in a simple lattice model with nearest-neighbor hopping ($t$) projected onto a constrained Hilbert space, analogous to the $t$-$J$ model with $J=0$, where kinetic magnetism has been previously studied. Using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on cylinders up to width $L_y=8$, we find a superconducting ground state exhibiting a key difference from high-$T_c$ cuprates: both the pairing gap and phase stiffness \textit{increase} with doping ($x$). We find pairing gaps, determined from spin and single-electron charge gaps, exceeding $1.5t$. This model can be realized within the double Kondo lattice model, relevant to bilayer nickelates, in the limit of strong inter-layer spin coupling ($J_\perp/t \rightarrow +\infty$) and a balancing inter-layer repulsion ($V$). Importantly, the double Kondo model does not fundamentally restrict $J_\perp/t$, suggesting the potential for high critical temperatures ($T_c$) approaching $0.5t$. While this idealized limit predicts large pairing gaps, we show a smooth connection to the more realistic regime with $J_\perp \sim t$, albeit with a reduced pairing gap of approximately $0.1t$. Assuming $t \sim 10^3$ K in typical solid state systems, our model suggests the exciting possibility of achieving $T_c$ of hundreds of Kelvin. We propose searching for bilayer materials with reduced out-of-plane lattice constants to better approximate the conditions of our ideal model.

items.title: Pair-density-wave superconductivity and Anderson's theorem in bilayer nickelates
items.summary: The recent experimental observations of high temperature superconductivity in bilayer nickelate have attracted lots of attentions. Previous studies have assumed a mirror symmetry $\mathcal M$ between the two layers and focused on uniform and clean superconducting states. Here, we show that breaking this mirror symmetry via an applied displacement field can stabilize a pair-density-wave (PDW) superconductor, which is similar to the Fulde--Ferrell--Larkin--Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, but at zero magnetic field. Based on a mean-field analysis of a model of $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital with an effective inter-layer attraction, we demonstrate that the PDW phase is robust over a wide range of displacement field, interlayer hopping strengths, and electron fillings. Finally, we analyze disorder effects on interlayer superconductivity within the first Born approximation. Based on symmetry considerations, we show that pairing is weaken by disorders which break the mirror symmetry, even with unbroken time reversal symmetry. Our results establish bilayer nickelate as a tunable platform for realizing finite-momentum pairing and for exploring generalized disorder effects.

items.title: What is a minimum work transition in stochastic thermodynamics?
items.summary: We reassess the concept of transition at minimum work in classical stochastic finite-time thermodynamics, when the system dynamics is modelled by a diffusion process. We show that a well-posed formulation of the optimal control problem corresponding to the minimization of the mean work done on the system during a finite-time transition necessarily requires taking into account speed limits on control protocols. This fact has major qualitative consequences. First, it permits to discriminate between optimal swift engineered equilibration and transitions at minimum work. Second, it shows that in the limit when speed limits are removed, only transitions specified by generalized Schr\"odinger bridges admit a consistent physical interpretation. To illustrate these points, we focus on the simplest model problem: a levitating particle in a Gaussian moving trap.

items.title: Origin of Reduced Coercive Field in ScAlN: Synergy of Structural Softening and Dynamic Atomic Correlations
authors: Ryotaro Sahashi, Po-Yen Chen, Teruyasu Mizoguchi
items.summary: Among wurtzite-type ferroelectrics, scandium-doped aluminum nitride (ScAlN) has emerged as a leading candidate for CMOS-compatible low-voltage memory, combining strong spontaneous polarization with process compatibility. A remarkable feature of this system is the pronounced reduction of the coercive field ($E_c$) with increasing Sc concentration; however, its microscopic origin remains poorly understood at the atomic scale, particularly under finite temperature and applied electric fields. Here, we employ an atomistic simulation framework that integrates a density-functional-theory-accurate machine-learning force field with an equivariant neural-network-based Born effective charge model to perform large-scale electric-field-induced molecular dynamics simulations at near-first-principles accuracy. The framework correctly reproduces key experimentally observed trends, including the decrease in the c/a ratio and the monotonic reduction of $E_c$ with increasing Sc content. Beyond static structural softening, we uncover a dynamic mechanism underlying $E_c$ reduction. Sc atoms exhibit larger thermal vibrations and begin to displace earlier during switching, acting as dynamic triggers for polarization reversal. Moreover, the displacement correlation between Sc and Al atoms evolves systematically with composition, enhancing cooperative atomic rearrangements and lowering the effective switching barrier. These results demonstrate that $E_c$ reduction in ScAlN arises from the synergy of structural softening and dynamic correlation evolution, providing a new perspective for designing hexagonal ferroelectrics.

items.title: Coordination-number dependent universality in Mixed Wet Percolation
authors: Jnana Ranjan Das, Santanu Sinha, Alex Hansen, Sitangshu Bikas Santra
items.summary: Mixed-wet percolation was introduced recently in the context of two-phase flow in porous media. In this model, the sites of the primal lattice are occupied with a certain probability $p$, and bonds are placed on the dual lattice between two adjacent occupied and unoccupied sites of the primal lattice. The occupied bonds on the dual lattice form perimeter bond clusters. We investigate here the scaling properties of the geometric quantities associated with the perimeter bond clusters of mixed-wet percolation on the dual triangular and dual honeycomb lattices in two dimensions. The perimeter bond clusters on the triangular lattice represent the boundaries of the site clusters on the primal lattice, whereas the perimeter bond clusters on the honeycomb lattice represent their hulls. Because of the low coordination number $z$ of the honeycomb lattice, the external and internal perimeter bond clusters remain isolated. Although mixed-wet percolation on the dual triangular lattice with a higher coordination number ($z=6$) exhibits ordinary cluster percolation, the model on the dual honeycomb lattice with a lower coordination number ($z=3$) exhibits hull percolation. Such a $z$ dependent crossover of universality in mixed-wet percolation is rare in the percolation literature. However, the external and internal perimeter bond clusters associated with a site cluster combine to form cluster envelopes. These cluster envelopes belong to the cluster percolation universality class.

items.title: Bootstrapping ground state properties of classical frustrated magnets
items.summary: We introduce a method based on semidefinite programming that produces rigorous two-sided bounds on ground state energy densities and correlation functions of translation-invariant classical spin models on infinite lattices. In this method, the challenge of non-convex optimization on an infinite lattice is replaced with a hierarchy of finite-size convex optimizations arising from positivity conditions that any probability distribution over spin configurations must satisfy. This adapts the Lasserre hierarchy in the theory of polynomial optimization to the context of frustrated magnetism, and we prove convergence of this hierarchy in the thermodynamic limit. Our method subsumes the Luttinger--Tisza method and further applies to non-quadratic Hamiltonians and non-Bravais lattices, thus addressing limitations of prior analytical methods. We apply the method to various two-dimensional frustrated spin models, where it brackets the energy densities and observables accurately across large parameter ranges with typical run times of seconds per parameter point.

items.title: Connecting Microseismicity to Lithology via a Model of Slip Avalanches
authors: Ethan A. Mullen (Department of Physics and Anthony J. Leggett Institute for Condensed Matter Theory, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, USA), Yanbo Wang (Integrated Multi-Physics Lab, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Utah, Salt Lake City, USA), Jordan J. Sickle (Department of Physics and Anthony J. Leggett Institute for Condensed Matter Theory, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, USA), Frank W. DelRio (Material, Physical, and Chemical Sciences Center, Sandia National Laboratories, Albuquerque, USA), Pania Newell (Integrated Multi-Physics Lab, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Utah, Salt Lake City, USA), Anastasia G. Ilgen (Geothermal Research Department, Sandia National Laboratories, Albuquerque, USA), Karin A. Dahmen (Department of Physics and Anthony J. Leggett Institute for Condensed Matter Theory, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Urbana, USA)
items.summary: Fluid injection into the earth's crust can induce small and frequent earthquakes in the subsurface. Predicting their sizes and temporal occurrences via statistical analysis is crucial for safe operations in unconventional oil and gas recovery, enhanced geothermal systems, and geologic carbon storage. Here we show that a simple micromechanical model of slip avalanches in slowly deforming solids predicts the slip statistics observed over drastically different spatial scales, namely meter-scale microseismic observations and nanometer- to micrometer-scale nanoindentation experiments can be described with this model. Microseismic catalogs extracted from high-pressure fluid injection operations into geological basins with various lithologies and nanoindentation experiments on shale across a wide range of temperatures and mineral compositions yield statistics consistent with model predictions. This universality across materials, temperatures, and scales is consistent with the prediction that the slip statistics result from only a few basic properties. Previously debated deviations of the statistics in layered sedimentary formations are explained by finite-size and stress-integrative effects resulting from mechanically weak bedding planes. The slip statistics therefore provide important information about the structure and scales of the bedding planes. Conversely, the basin structure can also be used to predict the probability distribution for the sizes of triggered microseismic events.

items.title: Universal swelling of tangentially driven ring polymers in two dimensions
items.summary: The interplay of tangential activity and excluded-volume interactions in ring polymers adsorbed to a surface, consistently results in the overall swelling of the ring configurations. This is in strong contrast to the case for three dimensional linear and ring polymers, where activity induces frequently collapsed structures. By means of Brownian Dynamic simulations, we investigate how the scaling properties of such active rings can be universally characterized by an activity-dependent Flory exponent, as a generalization of the equilibrium behavior. At high activity, an effective persistence length characterizes the conformations of active flexible rings.

items.title: Microscopically informed constitutive framework for stress overshoot, yielding, and strain hardening in amorphous materials
authors: Ankit Singh, Valeriy V. Ginzburg, Alessio Zaccone
items.summary: We develop a microscopic constitutive theory for the nonlinear deformation of metallic and polymer glasses based on nonaffine elasticity coupled to irreversible many-body relaxation. The theory predicts the full stress--strain response, from linear elasticity through stress overshoot and yielding to steady plastic flow. We show that stress overshoot originates from the competition between a nonaffine elastic instability induced by strain-driven loss of mechanical connectivity at the atomic/molecular level, and viscous dissipation associated with structural relaxation. For polymer glasses, finite chain extensibility naturally accounts for strain hardening at large deformation. The stretched-exponential relaxation exponent is obtained independently from stress or modulus relaxation measurements and provides the primary dynamical input to the theory. Using a small set of physically meaningful parameters, the model quantitatively reproduces experimental stress--strain curves for metallic glasses, polycarbonate, PMMA, and epoxy resins over a broad range of strain rates. These results establish a unified microscopic framework linking relaxation dynamics, yielding, plastic flow, and strain hardening in amorphous solids.

items.title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
authors: Huiyuan Zheng, Kaijie Yang, Ting Cao, Di Xiao
items.summary: Excitons possess internal structure absent from single-particle Bloch particles, allowing their band topology to emerge from the bound-state structure rather than being inherited from their constituents. This raises the question of how the internal structure of a bound state can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology. Here we show that the real-space embedding of charge-transfer excitons can generate an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals whose coupling supports topological exciton bands. Lateral electron-hole separation embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting its constituent sites rather than on either site. We demonstrate this mechanism in a honeycomb lattice, where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice. By solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, we show that this emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states. Our results establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases.

items.title: Random close packing at extreme size ratios with an Adam-based inflation protocol
items.summary: We present \texttt{rcpgenerator}, an openly available code for generating $d$-dimensional dense, disordered, non-overlapping close packings from an arbitrary prescribed list of particle diameters. The method adapts the Clarke--Wiley inflation protocol, but instead uses the Adam optimizer to relax the particle configuration. Typically, particle coordinates are advanced with a single, global step size, which must shrink as the size ratio $S\equiv D_{\max}/D_{\min}$ grows, generally stalling the optimization. Adam instead gives each coordinate its own adaptive step size, stabilizing the optimization time across a broader range of $S$. We demonstrate this in three-dimensional periodic tests that reach $S\sim5\times10^{5}$ for a continuous lognormal distribution ($N\sim10^{6}$ diameters) and particle numbers up to $N\approx5.6\times10^{6}$ for power-law distributions, with the densest packings reaching $\phi\simeq0.87$, each completed in minutes to hours on a multicore machine. Across truncated-lognormal, truncated-power-law, and Weibull distributions, the resulting $\phi$ reproduces trends such as the locations of peaks and knees with distribution shape and $S$ found in prior numerical results and in the parameter-free Farr--Groot prediction, with a remaining offset typically $0.005$--$0.01$. Additionally, results are commensurate with multimodal packing densities measured in vibrated-bed experiments. The code and the complete per-case census behind every figure are released with the paper.

items.title: Equivariant learning of a transferable three-dimensional classical density functional
items.summary: Liquids exhibit collective behavior that depends sensitively on thermodynamic conditions, interfaces and confinement, yet predicting each new state commonly requires a separate atomistic simulation. Classical density functional theory offers a reusable variational description, but its central excess free-energy functional is generally unknown, and learned approximations for fluids have largely been developed in reduced-dimensional geometries. Here we show that this functional can be learned directly from fully three-dimensional canonical equilibrium density fields while preserving spatial symmetry and variational consistency, without free-energy or chemical-potential training labels. A functional learned from coarse three-dimensional density fields remains predictive at finer resolution, separating the sampling demands of training from the spatial resolution of subsequent predictions. A single learned functional transfers across temperatures, system sizes and statistical ensembles, and recovers the equation of state, liquid--vapor coexistence and interfacial broadening, none of which are used as training targets. Applied to complex three-dimensional geometries, it predicts the potential of mean force between colloids due to solvent mediation, and adsorption isotherms in an interconnected gyroid pore. These results demonstrate that molecular dynamics equilibrium density data can be converted into a transferable thermodynamic generator connecting microscopic liquid structure to response, phase behavior and collective phenomena.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-based AI agents integrated with materials synthesis tools: the case of atomic layer deposition
items.summary: This work provides an overview of the different strategies that can be used to evaluate the performance of AI models and agents based on large language models (LLMs) for materials synthesis. After providing a brief overview of the key technologies behind the current generation of AI agents based on LLMs, we summarize the different approaches to evaluating these models in the context of materials science and in particular on materials synthesis, with a specific emphasis on scenarios in which the models are directly integrated with experimental tools. We discuss evaluation strategies spanning knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, tool-use benchmarks, and closed loop benchmarks involving the interaction with experimental systems or realistic virtual tools. We use atomic layer deposition (ALD) as a case study, emphasizing how existing approaches in the literature both build from general approaches used beyond materials science and can be generalized to other materials synthesis techniques. Finally, we provide a practical evaluation framework to evaluate LLMs in the context of materials synthesis

items.title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
items.summary: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. We use a heuristic mapping to compare the long-time kinetics of time-dependent and encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
items.summary: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed to infer a global average with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. Because the configuration is a single draw from equilibrium, a floor $R_n$ remains, and no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$. Before equilibrium, a certificate built on the displacement loses sight after about $\frac n4\ln m$ steps, half as long as the count of fixed cards in the same sample. At the two-dimensional Ising critical point the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$, with mean-field limit $\sqrt2-1$. For correlated fields, the usual 95\% interval can cover the ensemble mean in only 7\% of cases, and no bound on the floor from one realisation holds under stationarity alone.

items.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
items.summary: $XV$ ($X$ is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and $V$ is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (C$_i$) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of $XV$ centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of $V$ and C$_i$ in $XV$ formation. We find that $XV$ formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, $XV$ readily captures C$_i$ to form substitutional defect $X_s$, or captures an additional $V$ to form the complex $XV_2$. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of C$_i$ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of $XV$ centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

items.title: Native vacancies and antisites in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
authors: Tom\'as Rojas Solorzano (CICIMA, Universidad de Costa Rica, Sede de Occidente, Universidad de Costa Rica), Dale Igram (University of Michigan-Dearborn)
items.summary: Manganese selenide grows both as rock-salt $\alpha$-MnSe, a type-II antiferromagnet, and as metastable wurtzite w-MnSe, an antiferromagnet whose type of order is not known. In DFT+$U$, a spin-degenerate stripe order of w-MnSe lies 14 meV per formula unit below the A-type order, which is predicted to be altermagnetic. We compute the neutral Mn and Se vacancies and the two antisites of both polymorphs with a linear-response Hubbard $U$, between the Se-rich limit bounded by MnSe$_2$ and the Mn-rich limit set by the measured formation enthalpy. In $\alpha$-MnSe the Mn vacancy is lowest over most of the window (0.92 eV under Se-rich conditions), a candidate acceptor for its p-type conduction. In w-MnSe the Se antisite is lowest under Se-rich conditions, narrowly in the A-type order and, by an estimate, more clearly in the stripe order, and the Se vacancy under Mn-rich conditions. Changing the order shifts the formation energies by up to 0.26 eV, most for the Mn vacancy. Only the Se vacancy has nearly the same formation energy in both polymorphs; the other defects differ by 0.4-1.1 eV, although DFT+$U$ places wurtzite below rock salt, contrary to experiment. Three of the four defects leave an uncompensated moment of 3-5 $\mu_\mathrm{B}$. In the A-type order, band unfolding shows that the sign-reversing splitting of the most strongly split valence band, about 230 meV and 3 eV below the valence-band maximum (band-edge states are not resolved), changes its peak height by less than 8%, the resolution of the analysis, at 3% defects, while elsewhere the curve deviates by 18-45 meV (rms).

items.title: Thermodynamic Properties of the S=1/2 Zigzag Spin Ladder
authors: Nobuya Maeshima, Kouichi Okunishi, Toshiya Hikihara
items.summary: We investigate finite-temperature properties of the spin-1/2 zigzag Heisenberg ladder with an anisotropic off-diagonal $\Gamma$ interaction. Thermal states are calculated by an infinite time-evolving block decimation method combined with purification, while exact diagonalization is used to analyze low-lying excitations. The entropy is strongly suppressed at low temperatures inside the gapped phases, whereas it remains enhanced near several ground-state phase boundaries. For the N\'eel phase at $J_2/J_1=0$, the model can be mapped by spin rotations onto the exactly solvable XYZ chain. The thermal gap extracted from the low-temperature specific heat agrees with the exact one-spinon gap, while the finite-size excitation gap obtained by exact diagonalization is consistent with a two-spinon excitation.

items.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
authors: Hanbit Oh, Laura Classen, Daniel F. Agterberg
items.summary: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.

items.title: Metric random tilings: counted geometric disorder and its diffraction
items.summary: Random tilings gain entropy through the many ways fixed shapes can meet. What disorder remains possible when every face keeps its neighbours and every edge its direction? In metric random tilings, shared edges take discrete lengths that must close every face. For three equally spaced lengths, four of the eleven uniform tilings admit a number of geometries that grows exponentially with area. On the honeycomb this multiplicity survives even when the boundary and inventory of each flower patch are prescribed. Breaking the equal spacing lowers the estimated honeycomb entropy from about half a Boltzmann constant per face to about a fifth. Shifting all lengths together preserves every pattern and its probability, yet changes the coherent diffraction intensity by nearly three orders of magnitude on matched honeycomb samples. Metric random tilings thus realize bulk disorder at fixed topology and reveal how strongly its diffraction signature can vary at fixed configurational entropy.

items.title: Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
items.summary: Freidlin-Wentzell theory provides the quantitative foundation for rare, noise-induced transitions in metastable systems, predicting optimal transition paths, the exponential scaling of mean escape times, and the long-term occupancy of competing attractors. We present a pedagogical, physics-oriented review built on Feng-Kurtz's unified Hamiltonian framework: from the infinitesimal generator of a Markov process we derive the Hamiltonian, the Lagrangian and action via Legendre-Fenchel duality, and the quasi-potential. The same formalism covers weak-noise diffusions, Markov jump processes, interacting particle systems, and nonequilibrium stochastic fields. We show how broken detailed balance separates forward and reverse transition paths, and how W-graphs construct multi-attractor landscapes. Finally, we connect the theory to numerical methods, including ordered upwind methods, geometric minimum action algorithms, and neural-network parameterizations, and provide an accompanying GPU-accelerated Python package.

items.title: Twisted light affects ultrafast demagnetization
authors: Eva Prinz, Paul Herrgen, Jonas Hoefer, Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Irradiation with an ultrashort laser pulse can completely destroy the magnetic order of ferromagnetic thin films on the femtosecond timescale. This phenomenon holds great potential for ultrafast spintronics and information processing and is an active field of research. It is still an open question if the angular momentum of light can support this effect. While it has been shown that the spin of light only has a negligible influence, we experimentally demonstrate the influence of photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) on the magnetization dynamics of a thin nickel film. Our results reveal that the photonic OAM affects the demagnetization behavior by a non-coherent, secondary process within the first hundreds of femtoseconds depending on the handedness of the OAM with respect to the direction of the sample magnetization.

items.title: Glued tree lattices with only compact localized states
authors: Andrew Osborne, Ciro Salcedo, Andrew A. Houck
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Flat band physics is a central theme in modern condensed matter physics. By constructing a tight--binding single particle system that has vanishing momentum dispersion in one or more bands, and subsequently including more particles and interactions, it is possible to study physics in strongly interacting regimes. Inspired by the glued trees that first arose in one of the few known examples of quantum supremacy, we define and analyze two infinite families of tight binding single particle Bose--Hubbard models that have only flat bands, and only compact localized states despite having any nonnegative number of translation symmetries. The first class of model that we introduce is constructed by replacing a sufficiently large fraction of the edges in a generic countable graph with glued trees modified to have complex hoppings. The second class arises from thinking of complex weighted glued trees as rhombi that can then be used to tile two dimensional space, giving rise to the familiar dice lattice and infinitely many generalizations thereof, of which some are Euclidian while others are hyperbolic.

items.title: A Polarization Hall Effect in Hydrated DNA
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We report magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent transverse-voltage phenomena in hydrated genomic DNA. The sample is confined beneath a glass coverslip in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry and subjected to perpendicular magnetic fields, revealing sharp thresholds, staircase-like voltage plateaus, and oscillatory structures approximately periodic in inverse magnetic field. Fixed-field cooling reveals longitudinal reorganizations near 20.6 and 12.0 $^\circ$C, while a separate experiment shows large-amplitude transverse oscillations below approximately 12 $^\circ$C. Water controls and buffer-free DNA measurements support an association between the structured response and the hydrated DNA system. We propose a polarization-based interpretation of the transverse response, termed a ``polarization Hall effect,'' and discuss the observed regimes within a phenomenological framework of nonlinear dynamics and metastable configurations. These findings identify hydrated DNA as a soft-matter system exhibiting structured electrical responses jointly regulated by magnetic field and temperature.

items.title: High-Power Laser Drives Motion in Ultra-thin Photonic Crystal Lightsails
authors: Lucas Norder, Ata Ke\c{s}kekler, Richard A. Norte
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Laser-driven lightsails require reflectors that are ultralight, highly reflective and robust under intense illumination. These demands point to the thinnest reflectors that dielectric optics allows, photonic crystals, in which a perforated membrane thinner than the wavelength of light acts as a mirror. Such mirrors reflect by confining light inside the membrane, but this confinement also amplifies absorption, making ultralow-loss, tension-bearing materials essential. Stoichiometric high-stress silicon nitride uniquely meets both requirements, yet its ~1 GPa stress makes large, compliant structures difficult to release intact, and such sails have never been pushed by high-power lasers. Here we demonstrate millimeter-wide, 200-nm-thick photonic-crystal trampolines in this material, with 99% design reflectivity at 1070 nm and a static stiffness of 0.53 N/m. Radiation pressure displaces them by more than a micrometer within 50 microseconds. In air, they withstand several times the irradiance found at the Sun's surface, delivered as a coherent beam. Light reshapes the sail more than it pushes it, since modest temperature differences buckle the membrane and collapse its stiffness, so thermal deformation outpaces radiation pressure within milliseconds. The interaction and compliance that make lightsails movable also let light deform them. These results establish a testbed for high-power nanophotonics, directed-energy systems and light-driven propulsion.

items.title: Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We show that a diffusion model for lattice field theory can be trained by self-learning, without configurations from a separate simulation, and used as the generator of an exact Markov chain. Training starts from exact samples at $\beta=0$, and along a ladder of couplings the model's own chain at each coupling, weighted by the action difference, trains the score at the next. A Metropolis-Hastings test on each proposal and its noising path keeps the sampled distribution exact for any network, so that network errors affect only the acceptance and autocorrelation times. In the two-dimensional compact XY model up to $\beta=1$, on the high-temperature side of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, ladders at $L=4$ and $8$ reproduce exact and reference values of the energy density and helicity modulus at every coupling, and the generator trained from $\beta=0$ at $L=8$ has the same acceptance as one trained on an exact chain at $\beta=1$. The acceptance follows the relation known from hybrid Monte Carlo, with terms set by the number of noise levels and by the network error per site, and a network trained at $L=4$ generates up to $L=16$ when the number of levels grows with the volume.

items.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
authors: Arpit Raj, Johannes Mitscherling, Bj\"orn Trauzettel
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.

items.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

items.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.

items.title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79659-3 Four decades of satellite data show that repeated outburst floods from ice-marginal lakes beside a Greenland glacier reset its flow to a slow state for several years, acting as a natural brake on ice motion.

items.title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79791-0 Predicting where species live is key to protecting biodiversity. The authors present EcoVAE, a generative model that rapidly and accurately predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations, and identifies sampling gaps.

items.title: Author Correction: A sensitive red/far-red photoswitch for controllable gene therapy in mouse models of metabolic diseases
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79407-7 Author Correction: A sensitive red/far-red photoswitch for controllable gene therapy in mouse models of metabolic diseases

items.title: Retraction Note: Combination of PARP and KRAS G12D inhibitors enhances therapeutic efficacy by exploiting vulnerabilities in PDAC
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-80283-4 Retraction Note: Combination of PARP and KRAS G12D inhibitors enhances therapeutic efficacy by exploiting vulnerabilities in PDAC

items.title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79502-9 Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps remains challenging. Here the authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains from density maps.

items.title: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79540-3 CD33 and CD45 are both genetically linked to Alzheimer’s risk. Here the authors show the two proteins physically interact, and this interaction is increased in Alzheimer’s disease.

items.title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79338-3 T regulatory cells (Treg) cells may be involved with the regulation of immune responses in psoriasis. Here, using psoriasis samples from humans, the authors characterize the function of CD1a-responsive Treg cells in psoriasis and show that these cells secrete IL-10 in response to lysophosphatidylcholine and are found in close proximity to CD1a+ antigen-presenting cells and are potentially dysfunctional in psoriasis.

items.title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78734-z Photonic computing promises faster, more energy-efficient AI, but hardware scaling remains challenging. Here, the authors present HyperON, a TFLN-based hyperdimensional photonic computing network combining a spectral-spatial interweaver with wavelength-parallel modulators.

items.title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconductivity and Nontrivial Band Topology in Rock-Salt Transition-Metal Hydrides MH (M = Mo, W, Ru, Rh, Y)
authors: Yan-Li Zhang, 艳丽 张, Hao Ding, 豪 丁, Han Wang, 菡 王, Ya-Ping Li, 牙平 李, Jin-Han Tan, 锦函 谭, Na Jiao, 娜 焦, Rui Wang, 锐 王, Hong-Yan Lu and 洪艳 路
items.summary: Transition-metal hydrides have recently emerged as a promising platform for exploring the interplay between superconductivity and nontrivial band topology. Here, using first-principles calculations, we predict a family of rock-salt transition-metal monohydrides MH (M = Mo, W, Ru, Rh, Y) that are stable at ambient pressure. Our calculations show that these compounds exhibit phonon-mediated superconductivity, with estimated superconducting transition temperatures of 14.6 K, 14.5 K, 5.3 K, 7.9 K, and 4.5 K for MoH, WH, RuH, RhH, and YH, respectively. For MoH and WH, the electron–phonon coupling is mainly contributed by the softened low-frequency phonon modes associated with transition-metal vibrations, which couple strongly to the doubly degenerate d-orbitals ( and ) near the Fermi level. In addition, spin–orbit coupling opens nontrivial band gaps near the Fermi level, as confirmed by topological invariants and topologically protected surface states. These results identify rock-salt transition-metal monohydrides as promising ambient-pressure platforms for investigating the coexistence of superconductivity and nontrivial band topology.

items.title: Photoexcited Polaron Dynamics in Rutile TiO2 from First-Principles On-the-Fly Surface Hopping
authors: Chang Gao, 畅 高, Qijing Zheng, 奇靖 郑, Jin Zhao and 瑾 赵
items.summary: Photoinduced polaron dynamics challenges the classical path approximation (CPA), which prescribes nuclear motion on a single potential-energy surface (PES). To overcome this limitation, we use ΔSCF-based on-the-fly surface hopping involving both ground- and excited-state PESs to study photoexcited polaron dynamics in rutile TiO2. The simulations capture electron and hole polaron formation, migration, recombination, and subsequent ultrafast lattice relaxation. The electron–hole recombination lifetime increases by approximately two orders of magnitude relative to CPA-nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, from 38 ps to 6.3 ns. This increase arises from reduced nonadiabatic coupling: excitation-induced electron redistribution substantially changes the orbitals relative to the ground state at the same nuclear geometry. These results highlight the importance of orbitals associated with both PESs and lattice feedback in electron–hole recombination. The approach provides a tool for investigating excited-state dynamics in solids where the CPA breaks down.

items.title: Nonreciprocal Relaxation Acceleration
authors: Xingyu Zhang, 星宇 张, Yihan Ma, 艺函 马, Yue Liu, 越 刘, Niaz Ali Khan, Chenlong Huang, 晨龙 黄, Yuguo Su, 玉国 苏, JunYan Luo, 钧炎 骆, Dahai He and 达海 贺
items.summary: Driven by recent discoveries regarding the quantum Mpemba effect, the anomalous relaxation dynamics of open quantum systems have garnered significant attention. While expediting thermalization to equilibrium has been extensively studied, dynamically accelerating the convergence toward nonequilibrium steady states remains a formidable challenge. In this Letter, we find that a transiently engineered nonreciprocal dissipative channel can provide a shortcut that accelerates relaxation to the target reciprocal nonequilibrium steady state. Using a two-mode interacting bosonic model, we demonstrate that the temporal activation of a nonreciprocal channel efficiently suppresses prolonged inter-mode energy oscillations, enforcing a rapid, unidirectional thermal dump into the environment. Counterintuitively, under symmetric local dissipation, both nonreciprocal directions exhibit relaxation speedup with identical asymptotic spectral decay rates. Our results establish a route to accelerated nonequilibrium steady-state preparation in the studied bosonic model, with a covariance-based sufficient condition that extends to a multimode chain.

items.title: Kelvin-Temperature Ultracold Electron Beam
authors: Haoyu Huang, 浩宇 黄, Haibo Wang, 海波 王, Jianing Sun, 佳宁 孙, Enliang Wang, 恩亮 王, Xu Shan, 旭 单, Chunkai Xu, 春凯 徐, Xiangjun Chen and 向军 陈
items.summary: We report an ultracold electron beam with Kelvin-level transverse temperature generated from a cold atom electron source by two-color near-threshold photoionization of 87Rb atoms in a magneto-optical trap. A novel self-referenced scheme was employed to precisely determine its transverse temperature. In this scheme, a 3 × 3 beam array was generated to provide an in situ reference, allowing the transfer-matrix element to be determined directly from the measured grid pattern. The transverse momentum spread of the central beam at the source plane is then retrieved, yielding a transverse temperature of T = 2.0 ± 1.0 K, with the corresponding intrinsic coherence length of Lc = 21.1 ± 5.0 nm and a relative coherence length of C = (1.3 ± 0.4) × 10−3. The new scheme significantly suppresses the influence of residual magnetic fields, electric field inhomogeneities, and electron-optical aberrations. A non-monotonic dependence of the transverse temperature on excess energy was observed and was qualitatively explained by the simulation using a polarization-dependent single-atom Coulomb–Stark trajectory model.

items.title: Multiple Moiré Polarization Textures in Twisted Trilayers
authors: Haoshen Ye, Ying Zhou and Shuai Dong
items.summary: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moiré-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of the polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in certain twisted trilayers, where the relative moiré phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI3 and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, we clarify how the relative moiré phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture via layer sliding. The multiple moiré polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moiré patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

items.title: Ion pair acceptor electrolyte for high-energy Li-rich batteries
items.summary: Abstract Anion-derived inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphases (CEIs) offer a promising solution for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, conventional electrolytes struggle to suppress parasitic side reactions at the high-voltage cathode interface. Herein, a principle for ion pair acceptor electrolyte (IPAE) is proposed utilizing phosphazene-based molecules. Leveraging both anion- π and ion-dipole interactions, tailored (trifluoroethoxy)pentafluorocyclotriphosphazene (TFPN) interacts moderately with Li + and anions. These coordinations promote the formation of compact Li⁺-TFPN-anion nano-clusters in the electrolyte and facilitate a uniform, thin CEI during initial charging. The resulting interphase alleviates oxygen evolution and inhibits surface structural degradation, enabling the lithium-rich battery with 80% capacity retention over 1000 cycles. Furthermore, the IPAE enables a high energy density of 514 Wh kg −1 in a Li||LLO pouch cell with stable cycling. This work establishes a general design principle for high-performance electrolytes and an effective interphase engineering strategy for high-energy-density batteries with extended cycle life.

items.title: Quantum-geometry-tuned Mott transition and emergent heavy fermions in a topological flat band
items.summary: A flat band with a nonzero Chern number has no localized Wannier orbitals, which raises the question of whether Mott physics is still possible. We place a Hubbard interaction $U$ on coherent orbitals, which are localized but overcomplete, and develop a single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for this model. Within the flat band alone, DMFT reproduces the experimentally observed cascade and inverse-compressibility sawtooth without invoking Dirac revival or remote-band electrons. At nonzero integer filling we find an insulator-to-metal transition tuned by $s^2$, the fraction of the Brillouin zone that carries the Berry curvature. For $N_f=8$ flavors the Mott transition at $ν=-2$ occurs at $s^2_c\approx0.025$, where the top of the lower Hubbard band reaches the Fermi level and the local moments are Kondo screened, forming a heavy Fermi liquid (HFL). The HFL extends to the hole-doped side, $ν=-2-x$, but above the small Kondo temperature $T_K$ the state is an incoherent bad metal without a Fermi surface. At low temperature, an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A\sim0.1U$ replaces the HFL with a pseudogap metal that has a small Fermi surface and is dominated by spin-polaron excitations at small $x$. We propose this pseudogap metal as the parent state of superconductivity in TBG. The framework may also be applied to other topological bands, such as those of twisted WSe$_2$.

items.title: A Fractional Chern Semimetal: Exact Wavefunction and Conformal Criticality
items.summary: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.

items.title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
items.summary: Inverse problems for stiff parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs), such as the inverse heat conduction problem (IHCP), are severely ill-posed: the forward map rapidly damps high-frequency interior structure before it reaches the boundary. Soft-constrained physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which embed the PDE as a residual penalty, decouple the diffusivity from the surface data in their standard two-network inverse formulation, and the evaluated variants fit boundary measurements while leaving the interior field essentially untouched. We propose Neural Field Thermal Tomography (NeFTY), a hard-constrained neural field framework for label-free three-dimensional inverse heat conduction. NeFTY represents the unknown diffusivity as a continuous coordinate-based neural network, and at every optimization step passes the candidate field through a differentiable implicit-Euler heat solver with harmonic-mean interface flux, so that the simulated temperature satisfies the discretized heat equation up to the solver tolerance. Adjoint gradients propagate the surface reconstruction error back to the network weights at solver-level memory cost, making test-time inversion tractable on a single GPU. Across synthetic 3D benchmarks, NeFTY outperforms soft-constrained PINN variants, a voxel-grid baseline, and classical L-BFGS voxel inversion through the same solver on label-free volumetric recovery, and it transfers to real thermography data, surpassing classical signal-processing baselines in both defect segmentation and depth estimation. Additional details at https://cab-lab-princeton.github.io/nefty/

items.title: Solute-Aware Stochastic Korhonen Model of Electromigration in Wide vs Near-Bamboo Al-Cu Lines
items.summary: We couple an evolving Cu field to the one-dimensional Korhonen stress equation on random grain maps for wide (10 $μ$m), narrow (3 $μ$m) and near-bamboo Al-Cu lines. Earlier random-microstructure simulations fixed the Cu effect, and most continuum solute models used prescribed structures with all Cu mobile; we join the two and let only dissolved Cu move, the excess staying as immobile precipitate. With $10^3$ maps per condition at 200 $^\circ$C, we report nucleation times and sites, immortal fractions and Black's-law parameters. In cathode-limited lines Cu depletion shortens the median nucleation time 1.15- to 1.20-fold relative to immobile Cu for the cited Cu diffusivity; treating all Cu as mobile overstates this a further 2.24- to 2.36-fold at 2 wt%; the exponent stays near 2. In wide lines with reservoir ends, Cu steps left by the immobile precipitate become the failure sites, removing their Cu-free immortality if a quarter or more of the precipitate blocks Al diffusion.
