With Cu above the solvus the lifetime is not Arrhenius, as the dissolved fraction rises with temperature: a Black's-law fit at 250 to 300 $^\circ$C overestimates the median nucleation time at 150 $^\circ$C up to 2.33-fold at 2 wt% Cu with an exponent near 2. At the test durations the model qualitatively matches the cathode-side damage in narrow lines and the Cu build-up and mid-line peaks in wide lines but not the cathode-side Cu peaks or longer lives of narrow lines.

items.title: Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
items.summary: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

items.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP via III-V Buffer Layers
items.summary: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. We grow 151-nm thick PbSe films by molecular beam epitaxy on 200-nm thick In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As buffers on (001) InP substrates. Reflection high-energy electron diffraction and X-ray diffraction show (001)-oriented rock-salt PbSe with an out-of-plane lattice constant of 6.12 Angstrom on both buffers. Photoluminescence (PL) is observed from room-temperature down to 12 K and the peak wavelength red-shifts from 3.7 to 5.0 microns. Under identical measurement conditions, the room-temperature peak PL intensities from films on In0.53Ga0.47As and In0.52Al0.48As are approximately 1.9x and 1.3x that of a PbSe on GaAs substrate reference, respectively. These results establish an InP-compatible platform for integrating narrow band-gap PbSe with a broad range of ternary and quaternary III-V alloys, including, for example, structures in which In0.53Ga0.47As serves as both a short-wave infrared absorber and a template for PbSe growth.

items.title: Composition-dependent nonlinear viscoelastic-viscoplastic behavior and constitutive framework for digitally mixed polymers spanning the glass transition
items.summary: Multi-material PolyJet printing produces voxel-scale digital mixtures of an elastomeric photopolymer (Agilus) and a glassy photopolymer (Vero), giving a material family whose room-temperature response ranges from elastomeric to glassy. Large-deformation uniaxial compression over nearly three orders of magnitude in strain rate reveals a nonlinear, rate-dependent load-unload response that evolves continuously with composition, from recoverable elastomeric hysteresis to glassy yield with post-yield softening, hardening, and substantial residual strain. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) shows that each mixture has a single glass transition temperature ($T_g$) that shifts to higher temperature with both Vero fraction and frequency, so composition acts much as temperature or loading rate does. This time-composition equivalence motivates one constitutive structure for the whole family: an equilibrium hyperelastic network with three non-equilibrium, rate-dependent branches carrying reptational, intermolecular, and glassy resistance. Its properties are anchored at the two endpoints and interpolated by smooth composition scaling laws. The model captures the compression response of all seven calibrated compositions and predicts a withheld mixture from the scaling laws alone, as well as the plane-strain compression and uniaxial tension responses of three representative compositions. Resolving the predicted stress into its branches shows the load passing from the elastomeric to the glassy mechanism, and the work from elastic storage to dissipation, as Vero content and rate rise. The glass transition that DMA maps at small strain therefore governs the large-strain deformation mechanisms. The framework gives a compact, physically based description of digitally mixed polymers and a predictive basis for designing functionally graded, architected multi-material structures.

items.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
items.summary: A systematic study of chiral effects is presented using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established, beyond the identification of their coefficients. In particular, we can appreciate how these effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. The consistent and covariant anomalies are both encapsulated in master formulae for the currents which result from a careful treatment of the regularisation. It is finally found that, at finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.

items.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
items.summary: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.

items.title: Anomalous Field-induced Coherence beyond Single-ion Kondo Physics
items.summary: The emergence of coherent heavy quasiparticles in Kondo lattices is generally accompanied by a reduction in electrical resistivity at low temperatures. However, certain strongly correlated metals exhibit anomalously large resistivities that persist to very low temperatures, raising fundamental questions about the mechanisms governing charge transport. Here, we report an unusual magnetic field-induced evolution of electronic transport and thermodynamic properties in a Ce-based heavy fermion compound, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$. At zero field, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ undergoes a magnetic transition at $T$$_{0}$ = 0.45 K and exhibits a strongly enhanced low temperature specific heat coefficient, reaching $C$/$T$ = 2.2 J/mol$_{Ce}$-K$^{2}$, but no discernible coherence in its electrical resistivity. Remarkably, applying a magnetic field produces a large negative magnetoresistance and restores coherent metallic behavior, characterized by low-temperature $T$$^2$ resistivity. Although the field dependence of the electronic specific heat coefficient can be described phenomenologically within a single-ion Kondo framework, the same description fails to account for the strong suppression of the residual resistivity and the overall magnetoresistance. These results point to an additional field-sensitive scattering contribution beyond conventional single-ion Kondo physics. The striking resemblance to the long-standing anomalous magnetotransport behavior of UBe$_{13}$, without the complications introduced by superconductivity, establishes Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ as a platform for investigating the microscopic origin of anomalous scattering and field-induced coherent transport in strongly correlated electron systems.

items.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
items.summary: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

items.title: Surface Nanometal Enables Fast and Hysteresis-Free Optical Hydrogen Detection
authors: Jiamai Ren, Zeliu Li, Xiaotong Li, Yu Guo, Wen Yan, Dawei Li, Fu Zheng, Xinpu Zhang, and Wei Peng
items.summary: Abstract Palladium’s path-dependent hydrogen absorption/desorption and phase-transition kinetics result in hysteresis and nonlinear responses, thereby compromising signal fidelity and repeatability. Herein, we propose and demonstrate a surface nanometal strategy using Au or Pt nanoclusters to regulate hydrogen diffusion. In particular, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that surface-deposited Pt nanoclusters act as cocatalysts, modulating interfacial electronic structure, accelerating H 2 dissociation, and promoting hydrogen spillover. This increases surface hydrogen chemical potential and eliminates absorption/desorption barrier asymmetry. For the fiber sensor with a 6.8 nm Pd film and 1.84 atomic % Pt loading, a 15 s response time and merely 2.21% maximum hysteresis error are achieved at 3.5% H 2 concentration. Further increasing Pt loading to 4.17 atomic % makes the hysteresis error negligible (only 0.32%), nearly achieving ideal hysteresis-free sensing behavior. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that surface nanometal is an efficient strategy for hysteresis suppression while maintaining rapid sensing response.

items.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
items.summary: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (Péclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

items.title: Self-similar Inequality Dynamics in Biased Competition for a Conserved Resource
items.summary: In many complex systems the redistribution of a conserved resource can generate strong inequality. Important examples are cities exchanging inhabitants, farms competing for farmland, or agents for wealth in saturated markets. Here we model such systems as agents competing for a fixed total resource, and show that coupling agent extinction to a bias favoring richer agents dynamically amplifies this inequality over time. Drawing on an analogy with emulsions, where droplets compete for a conserved quantity, we introduce a dynamical critical resource size that determines an agent's fate. Crucially, this threshold grows in time, continuously raising the bar for survival and further reinforcing inequality. Increasing the bias strength, we find a transition from a continuous resource concentration towards a winner-takes-all outcome. Furthermore, the case of continuous resource concentration is characterized by a self-similar dynamics accompanied by a power-law or exponential increase in inequality, quantified by the Gini coefficient. We derive these results analytically in a mean-field model and compare them to agent-based simulations, showing excellent agreement.

items.title: Lincege.jl: LINked Cluster Expansions on a GEneral GEometry
items.summary: The numerical linked-cluster expansion (NLCE) is a powerful tool for studying properties of quantum lattice models directly in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we introduce Lincege.jl, a versatile, efficient, and easy-to-use package for generating the clusters needed to perform the NLCE on a general finite or infinite lattice. Lincege.jl takes as input only the Bravais lattice vectors, the basis information, and the expansion unit and uses a depth-first search to efficiently generate clusters, their lattice constants, and the sub-cluster information. It outputs final coefficients of the series, expressed in terms of the extensive properties of the clusters, in different orders. The package also contains tools for visualizing the lattice and the generated clusters as well as a classical Ising model solver that can be used as a template for interfacing Lincege.jl with solvers of other lattice models. This package can be installed using the Julia package manager and utilized with example scripts from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/rightleftspin/Lincege.jl. The online documentation, including examples, can be found at https://rightleftspin.github.io/Lincege.jl/stable/.

items.title: Quantum and classical transport in the underscreened Kondo lattice
items.summary: We investigate quantum effects in high-spin Kondo-lattice transport as resistivity approaches the classical spin-disorder limit. Using dynamical mean-field theory and the numerical renormalization group, we calculate resistivity, the Seebeck coefficient, and optical conductivity for the paramagnetic single-channel Kondo lattice away from half filling. At intermediate temperatures, the resistivity for large local spin $S$ approaches the double-exchange plateau. Thermopower retains a positive quantum excess even where resistivity is nearly classical. The excess arises from the transport kernel's particle-hole asymmetry. Even the full Kelvin approximation, often accurate for incoherent correlated metals, captures only part of it. Incomplete Kondo screening leaves residual moments and leads to singular Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. For $S=1$, the apparent power-law resistivity is consistent with a $1/\ln^2(T_ρ/T)$ asymptote. Above the Kondo scale $T_K$, weak-coupling resistivity follows $1/\ln^2(T/T_K)$. Above the band and exchange scales, the charge susceptibility decreases as $1/T$, while the effective diffusion constant becomes nearly temperature independent, resulting in linear resistivity. A many-body coherent-potential approximation accounts for the spin dependence of the linear coefficient without adjustable parameters.

items.title: Dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
items.summary: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on Rényi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for Rényi-2. Focusing on Rényi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ansätze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher Rényi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of Rényi evolution in deterministic systems.

items.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For a Multi-Phase Alternating Renewal Random Walk
items.summary: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TURs) impose universal bounds linking current precision to entropy production in nonequilibrium systems. While general bounds like the Proesmans--Van den Broeck (PV) relation provide a broad framework, they often remain loose for processes characterized by renewal events. In this work, we derive a generalized entropic bound for current fluctuations in renewal-reward processes. By utilizing a rigorous variance decomposition within the framework of renewal-reward theory, we obtain a model-independent bound that is rigorous and, for a range of parameters in the examples considered, tighter than the PV relation evaluated with the total entropy production of the extended (position and heading) state space. Notably, in the linear-response regime, our bound correctly scales with the renewal rate and identifies a precision penalty arising from fluctuations of the cycle reward. These results provide a physically informative constraint on the precision of run-and-tumble-type dynamics and highlight the universal limits of transport in complex stochastic walkers.

items.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
items.summary: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $φ^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.

items.title: LeIFF: A localized-electron and ion force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics
items.summary: Classical and machine-learned interatomic potentials enable large-scale simulations by replacing electronic structure with an effective energy surface for nuclear motion. This excludes electronic dynamics, electronic excitation and energy exchange between electrons and ions. First-principles electron dynamics can describe these processes, but its computational cost restricts system sizes and simulation times. Electron force fields offer an intermediate description by treating electrons as semiclassical dynamical particles interacting with ions. We introduce the localized-electron and ion force field (LeIFF), a compact physical model for both ground state bonding and excited electron dynamics. Valence electrons are represented by spin-labeled spherical charge distributions with dynamical centers and widths. The energy combines analytic electronic kinetic, Coulomb, and dispersion terms with spline-interpolated short-range interactions fitted to a large molecular data set. The resulting energy surface describes a variety of ground state properties across diverse bonding environments and charge states. It also provides a qualitative description of electronic behavior away from equilibrium. It shows improved robustness, accuracy, and transferability relative to earlier electron force-fields. Without any solid-state training, the same model describes dielectric screening and collective electronic response in silicon. LeIFF thus opens a route to large-scale simulations of nonadiabatic processes in molecules and solids, combining chemical bonding and nonequilibrium electronic motion within a common physical framework.

items.title: Fast-erasure energy-cost lower bound and its first-order correction under restricted control
items.summary: Determining the minimum work required for information erasure is central to understanding the energetic limits of fast and reliable information processing. In the fast-erasure limit, we derive an explicit expression for this minimum work in a one-dimensional overdamped isothermal system with control restricted to linear and quadratic additions to a reference potential. For symmetric initial distributions at fixed mobility, the minimum work scales inversely with the erasure duration, with a prefactor determined solely by the second moment and a quantile associated with the target success probability. We further derive the leading finite-time correction at a prescribed success probability and verify both analytical predictions numerically. These results provide an analytical benchmark for fast erasure under restricted control, connecting a universal leading cost with finite-time corrections that account for the detailed form of the memory potential.

items.title: Self-consistent Floquet theory of steady-state ordering in driven open systems
items.summary: Periodically driven open systems have quasienergy bands whose steady-state occupations are set by the drive and reservoir. We formulate a self-consistent Floquet spectral theory of electronic ordering in the weak-reservoir-coupling limit, expressing the nonlinear mean-field equation and the particle-hole response in terms of quasienergies, steady-state occupations, and harmonic matrix elements that account for micromotion. We illustrate the theory in the square-lattice Hubbard model and show how the drive produces `dynamical nesting' conditions and how Floquet resonances produce \textit{hysteretic} responses due to multiple self-consistent solutions. Interestingly, we find that the hysteresis branches exhibit distinct Floquet topologies. Away from half-filling, we find that the combination of drive-induced detuning of the van Hove saddle points and the micromotion leads to the onset of switching between competing incommensurate orders.

items.title: Terahertz detection of magnon chirality in polycrystalline CsCuCl$_3$
items.summary: In antiferromagnets, the handedness of magnon precession is usually measured on single crystals. In a pressed pellet of the chiral helimagnet CsCuCl$_3$, whose grains carry both structural handednesses and all orientations, we found that, from 5 to 7 T, the sub-terahertz magnon absorbs one circular polarization more than 20 times as strongly as the other, which rules out precession about each grain's own axis. Spin-wave theory attributes this to the Zeeman frequency, here two to four times the exchange-enhanced gap, which locks the precession axis to the field in every grain. Magnon chirality in antiferromagnets is thus accessible without a single crystal.

items.title: Liquid-liquid phase transitions in dipolar liquids. Insights into Supercooled Water
items.summary: Dipolar liquids combine two coupled degrees of freedom, translational and dipolar. Intriguingly, these two sectors can reside in distinct thermodynamic states, with the state of one sector possibly favouring a specific state of the other. The onset of ferroelectric order in dipolar liquids is an example of this mutual stabilization. Since this coupling is often encoded in interaction potentials, projecting out one sector to derive an effective interaction for the other can uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying this phenomenon. A coarse-grained theory, solved in the large-dimensional limit, in which the distance between nearest-neighbour particles depends on their dipolar interaction through a density-dependent mechanical compliance shows that a ferroelectric transition can trigger a liquid-liquid transition. It also predicts a first-order liquid-liquid transition within the paraelectric phase that, in turn, can promote ferroelectric ordering. The anisotropic dipolar-dependent soft-core interaction is shown to lead to an effective Jagla-like isotropic two-length-scale interaction, known to support liquid-liquid phase transitions. Here, however, the two-length-scale pattern depends on density and dipolar configuration, and is therefore sensitive to dipolar order. Analysis of supercooled TIP4P/Ice water molecular dynamics simulations shows that first-coordination-shell features of the pair correlation functions are sensitive to dipolar interaction, supporting the foundations of the coarse-grained theory. Comparison of low- and high-density liquid water reveals enhanced spatial anisotropy of the first coordination shell in the low-density liquid, associated, within the theory, with increased effective excluded volume, showing that the liquid-liquid transition involves structural changes within the first shell, beyond reorganization of the interstitial region and tetrahedral order.

items.title: Magnetism and symmetry of superconducting gap in LaFeAsO from dynamical mean-field theory
items.summary: By employing a combined method of density functional theory and dynamical mean field theory (DFT+DMFT) we investigate the effect of electronic correlations on the magnetic and superconducting properties of the iron-based parent compound LaFeAsO. We find that the static non-local susceptibility $χ({\bf q})$ and the dynamical spin structure factor $S({\mathbf q},ω)$ exhibit a peak at the in-plane wave vector ${\mathbf Q}=(π,π)$, which is strongly enhanced upon inclusion of dynamical vertex corrections in the ladder approximation, leading to magnetic instability. Considering the eigenfunctions of the Bethe-Salpeter equation with the vertex, obtained within the second order perturbation theory, as well as the ladder approach containing dynamic interaction vertices, in agreement with earlier weak-coupling-based studies of LaFeAsO, we obtain a close competition between $d$-wave and $s_{\pm}$ order parameters, dominating in the second-order and ladder approach, respectively. We argue that the dominating $s_{\pm}$ instability in the ladder DFT+DMFT approach is related to the reduced degree of magnetic frustration by itinerant degrees of freedom due to only partially formed local magnetic moments. Our study shows that dynamic correlation effects do not change the type of the leading superconducting instability in LaFeAsO.

items.title: Analytical Floquet Quantum Statistics from Nonequilibrium Green's Functions
items.summary: We derive an analytical expression for the steady-state quantum statistics of periodically driven quantum systems coupled to a bath using the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. By embedding Floquet theory into NEGF, we obtain closed expressions for the retarded, advanced, and lesser Green's functions in the Floquet representation, yielding the Floquet Fermi distribution in which the steady-state occupation is expressed as a weighted sum of Fermi functions evaluated at energies shifted by integer multiples of the driving frequency. The weights are determined solely by the Fourier components of the micromotion operator, providing a transparent interpretation of Floquet sideband occupations. We extend the analysis beyond diagonal commuting Hamiltonians treated previously, and derive the off-diagonal decoherences that arise under degeneracies. We further show that the robust Floquet distribution remains valid for a broad class of weakly coupled bath spectral functions beyond the ideal featureless-bath approximation. Finally, we establish a Floquet version of the Landauer formula for the DC part of the current, in which the equilibrium Fermi functions are replaced by their Floquet-modified counterparts. Together, these results provide a coherent description of Floquet quantum statistics and transport in periodically driven open quantum systems.

items.title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
items.summary: Interfaces between dissimilar two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a route to engineer electromechanical responses that are not intrinsic to the individual constituent layers. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate 461 van der Waals heterostructures constructed from 57 2D monolayers and establish a materials-design framework linking work-function mismatch, interfacial charge redistribution, dipole formation, and strain-dependent electromechanical response. We find that heterostructure formation generates out-of-plane interfacial dipoles via charge redistribution between the constituent layers, while biaxial in-plane strain systematically modulates them. The resulting heterostructures exhibit two distinct regimes: metallic interfaces with strain-tunable interfacial dipoles and semiconducting heterostructures with well-defined piezoelectric responses. For the latter, Berry-phase (BP) calculations independently validate the charge-density-difference (CDD) approach, which is generally applicable to all representative systems, with piezoelectric coefficients calculated via two methods agreeing to within 10%. Among 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reach 83.35 pCm-1 . These results demonstrate that the interface can serve as the active element governing electromechanical coupling and provide a computationally guided strategy for designing strain-tunable out-of-plane electromechanical responses in 2D van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Magneto-ARPES as a direct probe of Berry Curvature and the Orbital Magnetic Moment
items.summary: The Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment are central to the understanding of electronic transport phenomena such as the anomalous Hall effect, yet measuring these quantities directly with momentum resolution remains experimentally challenging. Here we show that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements in a weak magnetic field (magneto-ARPES) provide a direct route to both quantities. We develop an analytic theory of photoemission in a weak magnetic field and show that, for any material, the first-order change in photoemission intensity is directly proportional to both the Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment, even in the presence of self-energy effects. For linearly polarised light, the matrix elements are unchanged to first order in the field, so the intensity change directly reflects these quantities. Using monolayer WSe$_2$ as an example, we show how both quantities can be extracted in a typical experiment. This finding thus points to magneto-ARPES as a general route for measuring the momentum-resolved Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment in quantum materials.

items.title: Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo Simulations with Fast Ewald Summation for Calculating Individual Ionic Chemical Potentials
items.summary: We present a Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation method using fast Ewald summation to accurately and efficiently calculate the individual ionic excess chemical potentials of $α_+:α_-$ electrolyte solutions. By introducing a dynamic inner electrostatic potential that acts to penalize net charge fluctuations and maintain average charge neutrality ($\langle Q_t \rangle = 0$), the method enables single-ion GCMC trial moves without sacrificing convergence speed or breaking thermodynamic consistency. Unlike the Widom particle insertion method---which suffers from severe phase-space sampling bottlenecks and requires separate virtual insertions for each ionic species---the Donnan GCMC protocol simultaneously yields the individual excess chemical potentials $μ_+^{\text{ex}}$ and $μ_-^{\text{ex}}$ corresponding to a resulting bulk concentration $c_b$ with rapid numerical convergence. Varying the reference activity parameter $c_r$ allows us to efficiently construct the complete $μ_\pm^{\text{ex}}(c_b)$ curves. Comparison with the Mean Spherical Approximation (MSA) demonstrates excellent agreement for size-symmetric electrolytes, while highlighting the failure of linear-response theories for size-asymmetric ions where electrostatic correlations and cavity effects become strongly coupled.

items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.summary: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.

items.title: Dirac-like bands and weak-field transverse transport in ABA trilayer graphene
items.summary: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. These features offer a potential route to detecting the band inversion and constraining several of the least established tight-binding parameters, such as the on-site energy shift for the dimer pair of carbons $Δ^\prime$ and the next neighbour hopping parameters $γ_2$ and $γ_5$.

items.title: Bridging electrode preparation and electrocatalyst performance with physics-based causal AI using Bayesian Structural Causal Models
items.summary: State-of-the-art artificial intelligence (AI) and Machine-Learning (ML) tools have not yet enabled rapid design of next-generation materials. Detailed physical understanding of how material properties affect device performance is required to advance materials development. For example, optimization of ink parameters for electrocatalysts has no known physical mathematical model and thus insights are difficult to translate from material studies to device studies. Herein, we demonstrate how to use the emerging AI tool, physics-based structural causal models (SCMs), to extract quantitative causative insights from complex heterogeneous electrochemical systems with small (n < 10), but multi-modal datasets. Our SCM quantitatively separates the role that varying the support-to-catalyst ratios and total material loadings plays on catalytic performance. The proof of concept model developed in this work enables root-cause-analysis on the cyclic voltammograms of manganese-antimony oxide oxygen reduction electrocatalysts on Vulcan carbon supports tested in alkaline media using a rotating disc electrode device configuration. Our computational causal analyses quantitatively disentangle how the catalyst performance is affected by the number of active sites versus the thickness of the electrode. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of SCMs with physical equations applied to electrochemical materials and their performance.

items.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
items.summary: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.

items.title: Statistical mechanics of noisy collisions in active matter: Dyson-Landau theory
items.summary: Active systems and other coarse-grained descriptions are often modeled by generalized dynamics, effective equations of motion that are not bound by the constraints of genuinely microscopic physics. In particular, these equations are generally stochastic on the smallest resolved scale. This poses a challenge to first-principles statistical physics, which usually derives emergent noise on larger scales from deterministic interactions. Here, we show how to systematically incorporate microscopic noise into kinetic theory in the limit of weak noise, i.e., high activity. By means of a Dyson expansion of the noisy free propagator, we derive the leading correction to the Landau kinetic equation for weakly interacting systems. We find that the common practice of combining a deterministic collision integral with the diffusive terms of the Fokker--Planck equation is the correct leading order. For dry aligning active matter, however, the corrections are non-analytic in the noise strength, as nearly parallel particles interact for arbitrarily long times. For noise that acts only during interactions, a minimal model of stochastic interactions, noise and collisions do not decouple: the leading corrections are odd in the coupling strength, partly logarithmically enhanced, and amount to an orientation-dependent effective noise strength. Agent-based simulations confirm the predicted dependence on the sign of the coupling. Even in this minimal model, the effect of noise on collisions can thus not be inferred from symmetry alone.

items.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
items.summary: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with $σ_{xy} \approx 6e^{2}/h$, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.

items.title: Origin of the tetragonal-to-hexagonal phase transitions in Fe-doped BaTiO$_3$
items.summary: Based on detailed first-principles calculations, we investigate the tetragonal-to-hexagonal phase transition in Fe-doped BaTiO$_3$. Free energy calculations confirm a crossover from the tetragonal to hexagonal phases at 2.7--6\% Fe on cooling from the sintering temperature, in agreement with experimental observations, where comparative calculations show that neither CaTiO$_3$ nor SrTiO$_3$ exhibits similar behavior under equivalent substitution. Furthermore, three possible mechanisms are quantified: oxygen vacancies shift the crossover concentration from 2.7--6\% to 1.1--4.7\%, Jahn-Teller distortions are confined to the tetragonal phase, both favoring tetragonal-to-hexagonal phase transitions; whereas the tolerance factor is reduced in comparison with that of pristine BaTiO$_3$ for reasonable Fe valence states, disfavoring the occurrence of the hexagonal phases. Detailed analysis on the electronic structure reveals that the charge redistribution induced by oxygen vacancy is strongly orbital dependent, with the added charge occupying the $d_{z^2}$ orbital.

items.title: Universal electrical transport of composite Fermi liquid to Metal transition in Moiré systems
items.summary: We study universal electrical transport at continuous transitions between a composite Fermi liquid and a Fermi liquid in moiré Chern bands at fillings $ν=-1/2$ and $-3/4$. The critical theory couples Dirac fermions at a boson Laughlin--superfluid transition to a spinon Fermi surface through Chern--Simons gauge fields. We derive the Ioffe--Larkin rule for the full resistivity tensor and solve a quantum Boltzmann equation at leading order in a large-$N$ expansion. Spinon Landau damping adds a quasistatic scattering channel with weight independent of the spinon Fermi energy. At $N=1$ we obtain clean-limit resistivity jumps $Δρ_{xx}\approx5.896\,h/e^2$ and $0.1274\,h/e^2$ at the two fillings.

items.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
items.summary: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

items.title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure
items.summary: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.

items.title: Properties of the skyrmion crystal in the Heisenberg triangular lattice with scalar chirality
items.summary: Skyrmion crystals have been primarily discovered under a magnetic field for materials with noncentrosymmetric interactions. More recent developments have investigated the stability of skyrmion crystals in itinerant magnets without a magnetic field. In this study, we find that a type of skyrmion crystal with two topological charges per unit cell and no magnetization at the ferromagnetic point in reciprocal space, SkX-2, is naturally stabilized in an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric model with short-range interactions realized by the Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice with scalar chirality. We complement our numerical results with a theoretical analysis that quantitatively describes the transition from the ferromagnetic to the SkX-2 ground state and the evolution of the topological charge density. Despite the constraints given by the Mermin-Wagner theorem at finite temperature, the SkX-2 can either exhibit a first-order phase transition with translation symmetry breaking, or a continuous transition to a floating solid depending on the charge density, which is given by the strength of the scalar chirality interaction. Finally, the numerical results indicate the presence of $\mathbb{Z}_2$-vortices at finite temperature above the tetrahedral ground state in the antiferromagnetic region of our model, suggesting the existence of a vortex topological transition similar to that reported in the ordering of the pure antiferromagnetic model.

items.title: Adaptive Slater Koster Parameters: Crossing Oxidation States with Density Functional Tight Binding
items.summary: We propose to adapt the confined pseudo-atomic orbitals underpinning the Slater-Koster (SK) tables in density functional tight binding (DFTB) to local atomic environments. Assigning optimal SK parameters to metal atoms in different oxidation states improves the electronic structure of a partially oxidized Ni surface and, with adapted repulsion, Li insertion energetics in graphite. Their smooth, interpretable response to chemical and spatial environment, independently observed for Ni and Co oxides, enables a simple, physically informed machine-learning scheme, here applied to Ni-O binaries.

items.title: Strange correlator and string order parameter for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases in 1+1d
items.summary: We construct strange correlators and string order parameters for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases (NISPTs) in 1+1d spin chains. These diagnostics and the entanglement spectrum are connected to the interface algebra between two NISPTs. To compare phases, we first use finite-depth circuits of locally symmetric gates to minimize the bond dimension of each matrix product state. The resulting action tensors determine local strange charged operators and the charge decorations of truncated symmetry operators. The strange correlator probes the representation of the interface algebra realized by the two states. Higher-dimensional irreducible components yield nontrivial strange charged operators. For the distinct phases studied here, we identify such operators with long-range strange correlations. The full interface algebra admits a one-dimensional representation precisely when the phases coincide. For an on-site symmetry with a symmetric product reference state, the dimensions of the irreducible representations of the interface algebra also constrain degeneracies in the entanglement spectrum. We use unitary Drinfeld twists of a finite-dimensional Hopf $C^*$-algebra $H$ to construct general fixed point $\mathrm{Rep}(H)$ SPTs, action tensors and string order parameters. Our examples include the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ NISPTs and intrinsically mixed $G\times\mathrm{Rep}(G)$ SPTs with explicit Hamiltonians for $G=S_3$. For the self-dual Hopf algebra $A_{12}$, we construct Hamiltonians and string order parameters for the two $\mathrm{Rep}(A_{12})$ SPT phases and evaluate a strange correlator between them. We also outline a geometric extension to higher dimensions.

items.title: Giant dielectric permittivity in Nb-doped rutile crystals
items.summary: Dielectric properties of Nb-doped (~1.5 at.%) rutile single crystals were studied in the 10-300 K temperature range (at frequencies below the MHz range down to 0.3 K) in a broad frequency range, including terahertz and infrared range, to understand the origin of its giant permittivity. The results were fitted, modelled and compared with those of the undoped rutile crystal measured in the terahertz and infrared ranges. The primary effect originates from the near-electrode depletion layer of lower conductivity compared to the bulk (surface barrier-layer capacitor effect), which causes a strong thermally activated relaxation in the MHz dielectric spectra. In the higher frequency range, the main difference between doped and undoped crystals is the presence of an overdamped microwave excitation (central mode) in the doped crystal for both polarizations, persisting down to 10 K and not thermally activated. This accounts for the previously reported increased permittivity values down to 2 K - where all lower-frequency relaxations are frozen - compared to undoped crystals. It also explains why our low-frequency permittivity at 0.3 K exceeds its THz value. In similar Nb-doped rutile single crystals it was quite recently ascribed [V. A. Dinh et al., Phys. Rev. B 114, 024112, (2026)] to microwave tunneling of molecular polarons. Polar phonons are affected only by a slightly increased damping.

items.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
items.summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

items.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
items.summary: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

items.title: High-Stability Molecular Doping for High-Performance Tungsten Diselenide p-type Transistors
authors: Shiyuan Liu, Xiong Xiong, Xin Wang, Yuhang Chen, Ze Li, and Yanqing Wu
items.summary: Abstract Two-dimensional semiconductors offer a promising platform for next-generation complementary logic, yet high-performance p-type devices remain challenging. Molecular doping enables effective hole doping but often suffers from poor controllability and stability in atomically thin semiconductors. Here, we demonstrate stable and effective p-type doping of nontransfer monolayer and bilayer chemical-vapor-deposition-grown WSe 2 using 4-nitrobenzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate (4-NBD). The drain-current densities of monolayer and bilayer WSe 2 transistors reaches 368 and 798 μA·μm –1 at V DS = −2 V, representing 86% and 20% improvements over pristine devices, respectively, with pronounced threshold-voltage shifts. Meanwhile, the off-state current remains nearly unchanged, preserving an on/off current ratio of ∼10 8 . The doping effect remains stable up to 425 K and for at least 21 days after HfO 2 passivation, demonstrating excellent thermal and temporal stability. This work establishes an effective and controllable molecular doping strategy for high-performance p-type two-dimensional semiconductor devices.

items.title: Electrochemical Selection-Driven Reconstruction in Metastable High-Entropy Oxides toward Enhanced Acidic Oxygen Evolution
authors: Wuyong Zhang, Yun Liu, Yunxiang Wang, Haocheng Chen, Chaohao Cheng, Zhenye Kang, Tong Wu, and Zhiyi Lu
items.summary: Abstract High-entropy oxides offer broad opportunities for acidic OER catalysis, but their vast compositional space and dynamic evolution hinder identification of effective metal configurations. Here, we exploit harsh acidic OER conditions as an in situ selection field to direct the compositional evolution of metastable CrMnCoRuIrO 2 . Anodic polarization induces preferential metal dissolution and coordination reorganization, spontaneously forming a Mn- and Ir-rich reconstructed surface. The resulting A-CrMnCoRuIrO 2 requires only 162 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm –2 and remains stable for over 2000 h at 200 mA cm –2 in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 . In a proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer, it reaches 1 and 2 A cm –2 at 1.74 and 1.92 V, respectively, with 1,000 h stability at 1 A cm –2 . Operando spectroscopy, isotope-labeled mass spectrometry, and density functional theory reveal an adsorption evolution mechanism with balanced intermediate energetics. This strategy transforms electrochemical instability into a materials-selection force for optimizing complex multicomponent oxides.

items.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
items.summary: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.

items.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
items.summary: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.

items.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
items.summary: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with $α_\mathrm{R}\approx2$ eV Å in Ta$_2$CSSe and NbTaCS$_2$, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as $\approx28$ cm$^{-1}$. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching $\approx8$ cm$^{-1}$. Finally, we show external electric fields tunability over Rashba strength and chiral-phonon splittings, providing a common control knob for electronic spin and lattice angular momentum. Our work offers a unified strategy for realizing spintronic and chiral phononic in two-dimensional materials.

items.title: Construction of a Deployable Closure Model for the Transport of Turbulence Dissipation Rate with Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Machine Learning
items.summary: We present a hard-constrained physics-informed machine learning (PIML) method for constructing a deployable closure model for the transport of turbulence dissipation rate. The framework is built from modules, each performing a single task. The closure module represents the closure with a small network, while the state module represents the flow state during training. The closure network is coupled to the state network through the governing equation residuals. This coupling allows us to learn the closure without using reference closure values as training targets. The coordinate module learns monotone input coordinates that help both networks resolve sharp changes. Within the network architecture, the boundary condition (BC) module imposes boundary values exactly using the Theory of Functional Connections, and the realizability module keeps the closure realizable. We study decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) and learn $ψ$, the closure function governing dissipation rate decay, from trajectories obtained in experiments and direct numerical simulations. Here, the state module is a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), the BC module imposes the initial state and the closure's low and high Reynolds number limits, and the realizability module ensures growth of the Taylor microscale. The framework reduces the root mean square of the closure variation across ten random seeds by about 95\% relative to the unconstrained model over the training and held-out range. The deployed 18-parameter closure network requires only the Taylor scale Reynolds number $Re_{λ_g}$ and can be exported as a standalone C function.

items.title: Geometry-controlled clogging and transport mechanisms in confined Y-junctions
items.summary: We investigate transport and clogging of hard particles in a confined symmetric Y-junction using off-lattice Monte Carlo simulations. The geometry is controlled by the channel width w and a truncation parameter s that modifies the inner vertex. The flow probability exhibits a sharp sigmoidal crossover, defining a characteristic width wc that depends non-monotonically on s. This non-monotonic behavior persists under variations of the transverse Monte Carlo step, although the absolute values of wc change. Microscopic analysis reveals two distinct blocking mechanisms: single-particle obstruction at small truncations and collective arch-like structures at larger truncations. Residence-time statistics and particle-order inversions provide additional evidence of this change in transport dynamics. Our results demonstrate that local modifications of junction geometry can strongly affect clogging and particle transport, even in a minimal model with excluded-volume interactions only.

items.title: Critical escape dynamics of an active particle moving on curved surfaces
items.summary: On the macroscopic scale, active (self-propelled) objects moving through complex environments are often subject to effects arising from both the curvature of the surrounding surface and external influences such as gravity. We study the Kramers escape problem for active Brownian particles in two settings: motion in an external potential driven solely by gradient forces, and motion on a curved manifold subject to an additional constant gravitational force. In the absence of translational noise, a sharp dynamical transition occurs when the self-propulsion velocity $v_0$ reaches a critical velocity $v_c$ required for an escape. Above this threshold, the escape rate $k$ follows a universal scaling form, $k \propto \exp\left[-\mathrm{const}(v_0-v_c)^{-γ}\right]$, with an exponent $γ=3/2$ for the escape in a potential and $γ=1/2$ for the escape on a curved manifold in the presence of gravity. These distinct exponents reveal how the interplay of activity, surface curvature, and gravity determines the critical escape dynamics. Our theoretical predictions are verified by numerical simulations.

items.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
items.summary: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.

items.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
items.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.

items.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
items.summary: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation across different magnetic-field ranges without structural modification. This tunability alleviates the fixed sensitivity-range constraint of conventional tunneling magnetoresistance sensing, providing an accessible sensing range of +/-40 mT with an average probability sensitivity of 2.91%/mT. Importantly, the same stochastic switching process directly transduces magnetic stimuli into binary spike trains, integrating magnetic sensing, nonlinear rate encoding, and spike generation within a single nanoscale device. The resulting sigmoidal spike-rate response enables magnetic-field encoding, experimentally validated using the Neural Engineering Framework. Using experimentally characterized device responses, a simulated 10 x 10 SSN array achieves 90.7% accuracy in contactless magnetic-trajectory recognition with optimized encoding, approaching the software baseline. These results establish a scalable, MRAM-compatible approach to unifying programmable magnetic sensing and neural encoding for sensor-native edge intelligence.

items.title: t-J model at 50
items.summary: I briefly overview the original formulation of the t-J model starting from Hubbard model, as well as stress its unique features, i.e., advantages and shortcomings when discussing its physical properties. Particular emphasis is put on a brief characterization of connection between magnetism, unconventional superconductivity, and the Mott-Hubbard localization of the correlated carriers in a narrow band. In the second part I summarize the model generalization to the three--orbital situation. The main purpose is to list some basic features of the physics associated with t--J model.

items.title: Geometric Propulsion of a Scallop with Control-Dependent Hydrodynamics
items.summary: We study a force-free single-hinge swimmer driven by two controls. When its axial hydrodynamic connection depends only on the opening angle, we show that the mean displacement per cycle vanishes in the periodic state at any driving rate. An independent control of the hydrodynamic response removes this restriction. For a factorized connection, the displacement at arbitrary driving rate is an integral of a measurable shape moment against the hydrodynamic modulation; in the slow-driving limit it reduces to a curvature flux which, at fixed potential and connection, is independent of the shape mobility. A reflecting harmonic model illustrates how thermal fluctuations modify this flux without generating it, and a hinged-bead model with variable passive slip gives a quantitative opening--closing test of the mechanism. We distinguish these propulsion results from the leading shape-sector dissipation, which depends on the mobility and is governed by a thermodynamic metric.

items.title: The effect of isotopically-enriched 70Ge on the Raman scattering in Cr2Ge2Te6
items.summary: The highest-energy A5g Raman-active vibrational mode in chromium germanium telluride (Cr2Ge2Te6, CGT) exhibits a unique lineshape comprising a series of remarkably narrow peaks. While this multiplet was attributed to the natural isotope distribution of germanium affecting Ge-Ge pseudo-molecular vibrations, direct evidence has been lacking. Here, we present a Raman spectroscopy study of CGT isotopically enriched with 70Ge to validate this hypothesis. Upon isotopic enrichment, both the E5g and A5g modes exhibit a pronounced blue-shift. At room temperature, the A5g peak undergoes significant narrowing, while low-temperature measurements reveal a single, well-defined line instead of the previously observed multiplet. These observations align precisely with density functional theory calculations, confirming that the multi-line profile originates from Ge isotope distribution. Our findings demonstrate that similar isotope-induced Raman splitting may occur in other structurally analogous layered tellurides containing Ge or Si.

items.title: Strain-induced non-trivial band topology and large magnetoresistance in epitaxial SrTaO$_3$ thin films
items.summary: Epitaxial thin films of complex transition metal oxides constitute an ideal platform for realizing correlated topological phases through strain engineering of crystal symmetry and band topology. Here, we investigate the electronic transport properties and the band structure of the 5$d^1$ paramagnetic metal SrTaO$_3$ thin film under epitaxial compressive strain. The film exhibits a large non-saturating quasi-quadratic magnetoresistance (MR) and a nonlinear Hall effect characteristic of two-band transport, together with the field induced re-entrant metallic behavior. The violation of Kohler's scaling further corroborates the scattering from multiple bands. Semiclassical two-band analysis yields carrier densities and mobilities of the order $\sim 10^{21}~\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\sim 10^{4}~\mathrm{cm^2 V^{-1} s^{-1}}$, respectively. The observed large mobility and unsaturated MR, indicates the presence of a non-trivial band structure. Consistent with this, results from density functional theory calculations and tight binding model studies reveal that the stable structure has an octahedral rotation $a^0a^0c^+$, where the non-symmorphic symmetry ensures the presence of topological nodal lines yielding finite Berry curvature in the vicinity of the Fermi level. Besides the nodal line, trivial electron and hole pockets exist near the Fermi level, contributing to electron transport. These findings establish that epitaxial strain drives SrTaO$_3$ into a nontrivial topological semimetal, a phase inaccessible in the bulk counterpart.

items.title: Fluctuation imaging of disorder in monolayer semiconductors
items.summary: Monolayer semiconductors hold great potential for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and photonics. Excitons dominate their optical properties. As their electric fields extend outside the monolayer, they are sensitive to their surroundings. Thus, disorder can cause exciton instability, which is detrimental to device performance and critical for scalability and reproducibility. Here, we adapt a super-resolution fluorescence fluctuation microscopy technique to image localized exciton fluctuations in monolayer semiconductors, allowing us to identify unstable spots in an otherwise continuous monolayer with constant fluorescence. These spots correspond to interfacial disorder measured by atomic force microscopy. We examine how different material interfaces influence the fluctuations by comparing several substrates and provide additional insight into the disorder behind the fluctuations using hyperspectral imaging. We also assess the reduction of disorder upon thermal annealing, evidenced by a decrease in fluctuations. Our results show that fluorescence fluctuation imaging can detect disorder features similar to those of atomic force microscopy and hyperspectral imaging, while being faster and easier to implement. Therefore, it is a promising method for evaluating the quality of monolayer semiconductors, particularly when integrated with nanostructures and heterostructures found in nano-optoelectronic devices.

items.title: Coupled Altermagnetic and Valley Physics in Monolayer VBiSe$_3$
items.summary: The interplay of compensated magnetism, spin--orbit coupling (SOC), and valley degrees of freedom provides a promising route toward spin--valley control without conventional ferromagnetism. Here, using first-principles calculations combined with Wannier-based analysis, we reveal coupled altermagnetic and valley physics in monolayer VBiSe$_3$. In the absence of SOC, the compensated Néel antiferromagnetic state, whose opposite-spin V sublattices are related only by mirror operations, exhibits momentum-dependent spin splitting with a characteristic $i$-wave altermagnetic texture. Upon inclusion of SOC, the conduction-band states develop anisotropic Rashba-like spin splitting together with a sizable $K/K'$ valley splitting of about $112.2$~meV. Orbital analysis and an effective SOC Hamiltonian identify the hybridization between SOC-active Se-$p_{x,y}$ states and predominantly V-$d_{z^2}$ conduction-band states as an important microscopic origin of the valley splitting. The two valleys carry Berry curvature of the same sign but different magnitude, unlike the opposite-sign pattern of conventional valley Hall systems, so the large valley splitting, rather than a valley Hall effect, offers a possible route to valley-selective carrier occupation by gating. Moreover, a modest $-1\%$ biaxial compressive strain drives the system into a quasi-half-valley-metallic state with valley-polarized electrons and non-valley-polarized holes. These results establish monolayer VBiSe$_3$ as a promising platform for coupled altermagnetic, spin--orbit, and valley phenomena with strain-tunable electronic states.

items.title: Uniaxial poroelastic tendon model with crimped fibre recruitment reveals hysteresis
items.summary: Fibre recruitment plays an important role in tendon. Due to their large water content, a popular modelling approach for tendons is poroelasticity. Within this framework some tendon studies have included fibres, though none have included crimped fibre recruitment. We present a one dimensional poroelastic model in which the solid skeleton is composed of a soft neo-Hookean background matrix and crimped fibrils which do not bear load (FIB model). As the tissue is stretched, fibrils are straightened and contribute to load bearing. The fibre-reinforced tissue is compared to a tissue with a purely neo-Hookean (NH) skeleton in response to a uniaxial constant applied load (loading) and release of the load (unloading). The system dynamics are governed by a diffusion equation where the diffusion coefficient depends on stiffness. Within tendon parameter ranges, the FIB model is softer than the NH model, and so approaches steady state more slowly during loading. The presence of stiff, crimped fibrils increases bulk extension without excessively straining the fibrils, providing a natural protection mechanism for the tendon's structural components to load, in agreement with experiments. During unloading, the FIB model is much slower to relax as the tissue softens due to fibril re-crimping. This asymmetry in loading and unloading manifests as a hysteresis loop in the stress-strain curve averaged over the tendon. The hysteresis is reduced with increasing applied load.
